overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals is a regulatory municipal body responsible for adjudicating petitions for dimensional and use variances, special permits, comprehensive permits under M.G.L. Chapter 40B, and administrative appeals from decisions of the Building Commissioner. The board evaluates proposals for compliance with local zoning requirements, reviews architectural, civil engineering, and traffic peer analyses, and attaches conditions and mitigations to development approvals. The archive holds 46 meetings of the board dating from May 15, 2023, through September 24, 2026, spanning three municipal terms. Over this timeframe, the board resolved several major multifamily 40B applications and heard dozens of residential and commercial requests for alterations, additions, and change-of-use relief. At the most recent meeting, the board approved residential and commercial use petitions while continuing hearings on multiple accessory dwelling unit applications to review modified designs and consult legal counsel on state regulations.

threads.name: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway Chapter 40B comprehensive permit
threads.summary: The board resumed public hearings in May 2023 on an application by Case 40B-2022-01 to construct an eight-story, 350-unit development with 25% affordable units. Over several meetings, the board reviewed architectural and engineering peer reviews, fire safety and phased occupancy plans, security measures, and local preference options. The board determined that affordable units and commercial space were exempt from municipal linkage fees and granted a partial linkage fee waiver of $758,000 in consideration of off-site infrastructure upgrades. In July 2023, the board approved the comprehensive permit with conditions covering wood-frame fire safety, utility stretch codes, technical ordinance waivers, and an equity-led public art process. In October 2024, the board determined that proposed plan refinements—including shifting rooftop amenities and reconfiguring bike and trash storage—constituted insubstantial changes under 40B regulations.

threads.name: 970 Fellsway Chapter 40B comprehensive permit
threads.summary: In November 2023, the board opened hearings on a Chapter 40B proposal by The Davis Companies to construct a 289-unit residential project at 970 Fellsway and engaged peer reviewers for engineering, design, and traffic. The applicant submitted alternative site plans reducing building massing along Amaranth Avenue, introducing five-story step-downs, and adjusting site circulation to reduce traffic on Myrtle Street. The board conducted focused hearings on traffic studies, intersection safety, stormwater systems, EV charging stations, and architectural facades. In May 2024, the board determined the market-rate units were subject to Medford's linkage ordinance and voted to approve the comprehensive permit with an $816,564.24 partial linkage fee waiver for public improvements. In January 2025, the board approved an associated special permit allowing partial demolition of an existing commercial building on the property to accommodate a lot split.

threads.name: 280 Mystic Avenue Chapter 40B comprehensive permit
threads.summary: In April 2024, the board took up a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit application from Combined Properties to build an eight-story, 378-unit residential project with 25% affordable housing. The board authorized city staff to retain architectural, civil engineering, and traffic peer reviewers and to conduct direct working sessions with the applicant. In May 2024, the board found the applicant had not been responsive, set a deadline of June 6 for peer review fee payment, and continued the hearing. At the June 2024 meeting, the board voted to accept the applicant's formal request to withdraw the comprehensive permit petition.

threads.name: Accessory dwelling units and state regulations
threads.summary: In July 2026, the board approved a rear yard setback variance for an attached accessory dwelling unit (ADU) at 621 Fulton Street, but continued companion ADU applications for attic expansions at 1-3 Vassar Street and 12 Wellesley Street to review how new state zoning regulations apply. Both applications were continued again in August 2026 to ensure voting members could review previous hearing recordings. In September 2026, the board continued the Vassar Street and Wellesley Street applications to October 29, 2026, to allow the applicant to submit reduced designs and enable the board to obtain additional legal counsel regarding state ADU regulations.

threads.name: Cannabis dispensary permitting at 114 Mystic Avenue
threads.summary: In May 2026, the board approved special permits for Victory Gardens to conduct medical cannabis sales and product manufacturing at 114 Mystic Avenue. The applicant's accompanying request for cannabis courier delivery service was continued to June to obtain input from the police chief. The delivery service petition was continued again in June while awaiting legal counsel, and the board formally approved the special permit allowing cannabis delivery operations in July 2026.

threads.name: 590 Boston Avenue redevelopment relief
threads.summary: In May and July 2023, the board granted continuances and a six-month extension of prior relief for 590 Boston Avenue while the applicant coordinated site plan modifications with the Community Development Board. In November 2023, the board approved amendments to the variance and site plan for a five-story mixed-use building, expanding the residential unit count from 40 to 45 and shifting parking to an at-grade configuration with conditions. In January 2024, the board approved an additional six-month extension of the variance and special permit through July 12, 2024.

threads.name: Administrative zoning enforcement appeal for 91 Waterville Road
threads.summary: In April 2026, the board heard an administrative appeal regarding a notice of violation issued for operating a gutter business from a residential property, continuing the hearing after taking testimony from neighbors concerning truck idling and noise. In May 2026, the board formally upheld the Building Commissioner's notice of violation against Patricia and Paolo Wilder for operating a commercial business in a single-family zoning district.

citations.title: 91 Waterville Road: Administrative Appeal of Notice of Violation
citations.label: M42#1

periods.narrative: The board concentrated on comprehensive permit review for 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway, concluding with permit approval and partial linkage fee waivers. Members also adjudicated variances and special permits for residential additions, fence heights, and commercial redevelopments on Boston Avenue, while opening review on the 970 Fellsway development.

This period was dominated by multi-session peer reviews and the eventual approval of the 289-unit Chapter 40B permit at 970 Fellsway, as well as the withdrawal of the 280 Mystic Avenue 40B petition. The board also addressed residential conversions, board leadership elections, and administrative updates regarding rules and minutes procedures.

The board deliberated on municipal zoning enforcement appeals, permitted cannabis dispensary and delivery uses, and evaluated proposals for accessory dwelling units under evolving state regulations. Several residential conversions and additions were approved alongside continued legal reviews of attic expansion ADUs.
